risks: Revenue growth remains modest despite exceptional order growth, making conversion timing important.
Lower volumes and project timing can delay conversion even as margin execution remains strong.
Water scarcity can create demand for efficiency solutions but can also constrain project siting and customer expansion, so scarcity is not uniformly beneficial.
Backlog/order conversion can slip because large projects depend on customer budgets, schedules, performance requirements and supply availability.
The Evoqua integration broadens capability but creates continuing synergy/integration execution risk.
Connected measurement/control products increase cyber and technology-obsolescence exposure alongside their efficiency benefits.
unknowns: Durability and conversion timing of the unusually strong order intake are not yet established.
How much of current orders converts within 2026 versus later periods remains uncertain.
The share of the current order surge specifically attributable to AI infrastructure versus other industrial/municipal demand is not established.
Duration, cancellation protection and margin profile of the incremental order surge are not fully established by the current source set.
contradictions: Orders accelerated sharply while near-term revenue growth stayed low and full-year revenue guidance was narrowed.
Very strong orders indicate future demand but current revenue conversion remains modest; structural demand and near-term realization must not be conflated.

The order/revenue gap is real but not inherently adverse: it supports future demand visibility while simultaneously increasing the importance of conversion timing and mix. Treating orders as current revenue would inflate confidence.
